projectTitle: Void Studio: SDLC Office Materialization Simulator
deliverableJust: A browser-based 3D simulation allows students to experience the cascading consequences of decisions across all 6 SDLC phases in real-time. Unlike static case studies, players see their office environment physically materialize from a void — making abstract concepts like 'scope creep' and 'technical debt' tangible through visual feedback. The local AI Game Master (Phi-3.5 Mini, 3.8B parameters) generates contextual events that adapt to the player's resource state, ensuring no two playthroughs are identical.
problemStatement: In COM0463, students consistently underestimate the compounding effects of poor project management decisions. 72% of student projects in 2025 exceeded their original time estimates by >40%, and post-mortems reveal that students treated SDLC phases as isolated checkboxes rather than interconnected stages. Traditional lecture-based instruction fails to demonstrate that a requirements shortcut in Phase 1 causes exponentially larger problems in Phase 5 (Deployment). Void Studio addresses this by simulating the full SDLC lifecycle with resource management (Budget, Morale, Tech Debt, Time) where every decision ripples forward — and the visual consequence is an office that either flourishes or crumbles back into the void.
inScope: 6-phase SDLC progression (Requirements → Design → Implementation → Testing → Deployment → Maintenance)
3D isometric office materialization from void using Three.js
4-resource management system (Budget, Morale, Technical Debt, Time)
Dynamic event system with 15+ predefined scenarios and AI-generated events
Local LLM integration (Phi-3.5 Mini via WebLLM) for adaptive game mastering
Decision cards with visible trade-off impacts per option
Phase transition animations with office unlock sequences
NPC character system with mood-based contextual dialogue
Victory/Game Over conditions with score summary
Fallback mode for environments without GPU/WebGPU
outScope: Mobile native app version (browser-only for MVP)
Cloud-hosted LLM inference (all local via WebLLM)
Real financial data or production project imports

frs.desc: System shall simulate 6 SDLC phases (Requirements, Design, Implementation, Testing, Deployment, Maintenance) in sequential order with task checklists per phase.
System shall track 4 resource metrics (Budget, Morale, Technical Debt, Time) with real-time animated HUD bars that update after every action.
System shall trigger contextual random events during gameplay with 3 decision options, each showing predicted resource impacts before selection.
System shall materialize 3D office furniture and space from the void upon completing each SDLC phase, using particle effects and opacity animations.
System shall provide an AI Game Master mode using a local Phi-3.5 Mini LLM (via WebLLM) to generate dynamic events, evaluate decisions, and produce NPC dialogue.
System shall fall back to predefined event logic when LLM is unavailable, ensuring full playability without AI.
System shall end the game in 'Game Over' when any critical resource reaches 0% (or Tech Debt reaches 100%), displaying a post-mortem with final score.
System shall display a Victory screen with score breakdown when all 6 SDLC phases are completed successfully.
System shall provide a 'Consult AI' button allowing players to request strategic advice from the LLM about their current resource state.
System shall support NPC characters (PM Senior, Tech Lead, QA Manager, UX Designer) with personality-driven mood responses based on game state.

System shall log all player actions (task completions, event triggers, decision choices, resource deltas, phase transitions) to browser localStorage with timestamps for post-session analytics and instructor review.
System shall export a JSON session log file containing anonymised gameplay data that the instructor can import into the GPPT analytics dashboard for cohort-level analysis.

nfrs.desc: 3D scene shall render at ≥30 FPS on mid-range hardware (Intel i5, integrated GPU). The renderer shall degrade gracefully on WebGL-unsupported environments.
A new player shall be able to understand the HUD, execute their first task, and resolve their first event within 3 minutes without external instruction.
Game shall run in Chrome 113+, Firefox 115+, and Edge 113+ without plugins or installation. WebLLM requires WebGPU; game works without it.
LLM event generation shall complete within 10 seconds. If LLM response exceeds 30 seconds, system shall timeout and use fallback logic.
All UI text shall maintain WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1). Decision options shall be keyboard-navigable.

System shall comply with KVKK (Turkish data protection law) and GDPR principles: no personally identifiable information (PII) shall be collected or transmitted. All gameplay data remains in the player's browser localStorage. Session logs exported for instructor review shall be anonymised with opaque session IDs only.

Players shall provide informed consent via an in-game notice before any session data is logged. Players may clear all stored data at any time via browser settings. No data shall be sent to external servers without explicit opt-in.

successCriteria: 80% of students demonstrate improved understanding of SDLC phase interdependencies (measured by pre/post assessment)
Students who play 3+ sessions show ≥25% improvement in risk identification accuracy on course assignments
Average session completion rate of ≥70% (players reach at least Phase 4 Testing)
SUS usability score of ≥80 from post-session surveys
≥60% of players report that the game changed how they think about Technical Debt (qualitative survey)

sdtAutonomy: Players choose which risks to accept vs. mitigate at every decision point. They choose when to execute tasks, when to consult the AI, and how aggressively to manage resources. The open-ended event system means no single 'correct' path exists.
sdtCompetence: Progressive difficulty escalation across SDLC phases — early phases have forgiving events while later phases introduce compounding crises. The 3D office materialization provides concrete visual evidence of mastery. Score breakdown at game end gives precise performance feedback.
sdtRelatedness: NPC characters (PM Senior, Tech Lead, QA Lead, UX Designer) react to the player's decisions with mood-based dialogue, creating a sense of team responsibility. The AI Game Master provides personalized narrative feedback, making the player feel their decisions matter to 'real' team members.

mdaAnalysis.mechanics: Resource Bars (Budget/Morale/TechDebt/Time), Task Execution, Decision Cards with 3 options, Phase Progression, Office Materialization, AI Event Generation, NPC Mood System.
mdaAnalysis.dynamics: Risk-vs-reward trade-offs at every decision. Resource scarcity creates tension as players progress. The void-to-office progression creates an escalation of commitment. Compounding technical debt punishes shortcuts. LLM-generated events create unpredictable challenge.
mdaAnalysis.aesthetics: Challenge (managing 4 resources under pressure), Narrative (building a software company from nothing), Discovery (watching the office emerge from the void), Sensation (3D particle effects and materialization animations).

sixDim.what: A single-player, browser-based 3D simulation where players manage a software project through the full SDLC lifecycle. Each phase consists of task execution, resource management, and event resolution. Game mechanics include decision cards with trade-off analysis, progressive office materialization, and an adaptive AI game master.
sixDim.why: To bridge the gap between theoretical SDLC knowledge and practical project management intuition. The simulation creates a safe-to-fail environment where students experience the cascading consequences of PM decisions — something impossible in traditional lecture formats.
sixDim.who: COM0463 IT Project Management students in their final year. These are engineering students who value hands-on learning, respond to visual feedback, and are comfortable with browser-based tools. The simulation leverages their technical comfort while challenging their management skills.
sixDim.when: Deployed during Weeks 6-10 of COM0463, aligned with the 'SDLC & Risk Management' module. Each play session lasts 30-60 minutes. Students play at least 3 sessions across 4 weeks, allowing learning transfer between sessions.
sixDim.how: Isometric 3D using Three.js with no installation required. Resource impacts shown numerically before each decision to enable rational analysis. Difficulty adapts through event frequency — low resources trigger more recovery opportunities. LLM provides personalized feedback, but the game is fully playable without it.
sixDim.where: Browser-based (Vite + Three.js), accessible via any modern browser on lab computers and personal laptops. No server infrastructure required — all computation is client-side, including the LLM which runs entirely in the browser via WebLLM/WebGPU.

narrativeTheme: Void Studio: Building Reality from Nothing
narrativeArc: From an empty void to a fully-equipped software office. The player starts as a Project Manager with nothing — no team, no workspace, no tools. Each SDLC phase completed literally builds their world: desks materialize, servers rack up, monitors flicker to life. Failure means the void reclaims what was built.
characters: PM Senior (Mentor NPC, provides encouragement/warnings based on resource state), Tech Lead (Analytical NPC, reacts to Technical Debt level), QA Lead (Detail-oriented NPC, responds to Testing phase decisions), UX Designer (Empathetic NPC, tracks Team Morale).
storyWorld: A software company that exists in a metaphysical void — darkness, floating particles, and nebula gradients. Reality only exists where the player has built it through competent project management. The void is not hostile, but indifferent — it simply doesn't create things on its own. Only deliberate, well-managed development processes manifest reality.

introText: You are the Project Manager of a software company that exists... nowhere. Your office is the void itself — empty, dark, infinite. But with each step of the development lifecycle you complete, reality bends to your will. Desks materialize. Walls form. Screens flicker to life. Complete the SDLC. Build your office. Survive the chaos.

scenarios.name: The Requirements Meltdown
scenarios.title: Stakeholder Scope Creep
scenarios.setup: The primary stakeholder adds 5 new features mid-requirements phase.
scenarios.objective: Manage scope without destroying budget or morale.
scenarios.winCondition: Budget > 60% AND Morale > 50% after resolving all scope requests
scenarios.storyboard: Event Card → Decision → Resource Impact → Narrative Feedback
scenarios.outcome: Win: Office expands. Partial: Office partially expands with reduced furniture. Fail: Void reclaims.

activities.name: Negotiate scope reduction
activities.neutralCondition: Player negotiates partial scope reduction, preserving Budget > 40% but losing 2 features

activities.name: Accept all scope changes
activities.neutralCondition: Player accepts some changes with conditions — Morale drops but TechDebt does not increase

activities.name: Escalate to steering committee
activities.neutralCondition: Committee defers decision — no immediate resource loss but 1 day of Time consumed

scenarios.name: The Deployment Disaster
scenarios.title: Production Server Crash
scenarios.setup: Deployment to production fails. Server crashes. Client is watching.
scenarios.objective: Recover the deployment without losing the client's trust.
scenarios.winCondition: Deploy successfully with Morale > 40% and TechDebt < 70%
scenarios.storyboard: Crisis Alert → Emergency Options → Triage → Resolution
scenarios.outcome: Win: Ops center materializes with status lights. Partial: Basic ops desk without monitoring wall. Fail: Game Over.

activities.name: Rollback and hotfix
activities.neutralCondition: Rollback succeeds but hotfix introduces minor regression — TechDebt +5 but system stable

activities.name: Emergency all-hands debug
activities.neutralCondition: Bug found but fix requires overnight work — Morale -10 but deployment recovered

activities.name: Communicate delay to client
activities.neutralCondition: Client agrees to 1-day delay — Time -1 but relationship preserved

scenarios.name: The Technical Debt Avalanche
scenarios.title: Legacy Code Collapse
scenarios.setup: Technical debt accumulated from rushed Implementation phase causes cascading test failures in Testing.
scenarios.winCondition: TechDebt < 50% AND Time > 20% after refactoring sprint
scenarios.outcome: Win: Clean codebase, testing room materializes fully. Partial: Some tests pass, partial QA desk. Fail: Deployment blocked.

activities.name: Full refactoring sprint
activities.neutralCondition: Partial refactor reduces TechDebt by 15 but consumes 3 extra days of Time

activities.name: Targeted hotspot fixing
activities.neutralCondition: Critical paths fixed but secondary modules still fragile — TechDebt -10 only

scoringSystem.basis: Points calculated from remaining resources at game end: Score = Budget + Morale + (100 - TechDebt) + Time + (Phases Completed × 50) + (Events Survived × 10).
scoringSystem.bonuses: Perfect Phase: Complete a phase with all resources above 60%. Void Conqueror: Complete all 6 phases. AI Advisor: Use the LLM advisor at least 3 times.
scoringSystem.penalties: Technical Debt above 80% at game end halves the final score. Game Over (any resource at 0%) nullifies phase completion bonuses.
scoringSystem.badges: Void Pioneer (complete Phase 1), Code Commander (complete Implementation), Ship Captain (complete Deployment), Office Architect (complete all 6 phases), Chaos Survivor (survive 10+ events).

tuslerRisks.risk: Ignoring technical debt in Implementation phase leads to cascading test failures
tuslerRisks.preventive: TechDebt bar visible at all times with colour-coded warnings (green/yellow/red); events explicitly warn about compounding consequences in subsequent phases
tuslerRisks.responsive: Recovery events offer debt-reduction sprints at cost of budget/time; instructor can trigger manual debt-reduction event
tuslerRisks.mitigation: TechDebt bar visible at all times with colour-coded warnings; recovery events offer debt-reduction sprints at cost of budget and time

tuslerRisks.risk: Budget depletion before Deployment phase prevents completion
tuslerRisks.preventive: Budget impact shown numerically on every decision card before selection; cumulative spend tracker in HUD
tuslerRisks.responsive: Emergency budget events and contractor options available in late phases; instructor can inject emergency funding scenario
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Budget impact shown numerically on every decision card before selection; emergency funding events available in late phases

tuslerRisks.risk: Game is too difficult — students never reach Phase 4 Testing
tuslerRisks.preventive: Difficulty dynamically scales with resource state: resources below 30% trigger more recovery-oriented events; early phases have gentler event probability
tuslerRisks.responsive: Instructor can adjust base event probability in Events.js configuration; playtesting calibrates difficulty curve
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Difficulty dynamically scales with resource state; instructor can adjust event probability configuration

tuslerRisks.risk: LLM model download (1.5GB) blocks gameplay on slow connections
tuslerRisks.preventive: LLM is fully optional — game is 100% playable via FallbackLogic.js predefined events; toggle clearly visible on loading screen
tuslerRisks.responsive: One-time download cached by browser ServiceWorker; lab admin can pre-cache model on lab computers before session
tuslerRisks.mitigation: LLM is optional; FallbackLogic.js provides full gameplay; model cached after first download

tuslerRisks.risk: Students focus on 'winning the game' rather than learning PM concepts
tuslerRisks.preventive: Score formula weights all 4 resources equally preventing single-metric gaming; no shortcut exploits in event system
tuslerRisks.responsive: Mandatory post-game debrief discussion led by instructor comparing in-game decisions to PMBOK frameworks
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Score formula weights all 4 resources equally; mandatory post-game debrief links decisions to PMBOK

tuslerRisks.risk: WebGL rendering fails on older lab hardware without discrete GPU
tuslerRisks.preventive: Canvas 2D fallback renderer implemented with graceful degradation; game detects WebGL capability at startup
tuslerRisks.responsive: IT support notified to enable hardware acceleration in browser settings; software rendering fallback provides starfield visual
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Canvas 2D fallback renderer provides graceful degradation; game detects WebGL capability at startup

tuslerRisks.risk: Simulation events do not accurately represent real SDLC challenges
tuslerRisks.preventive: All events reviewed by course instructor against Marchewka chapters 6-11 and PMBOK risk categories before deployment
tuslerRisks.responsive: Event library updated each semester based on instructor feedback and student post-session surveys
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Events validated against Marchewka chapters and PMBOK; updated each semester from instructor and student feedback

tuslerRisks.risk: Student data privacy breach through exported session logs
tuslerRisks.preventive: No PII collected; session IDs are opaque UUIDs; KVKK/GDPR compliance built into NFR-06/NFR-07; consent notice shown before logging
tuslerRisks.responsive: All localStorage data can be cleared by student at any time; exported logs contain no identifying information
tuslerRisks.mitigation: No PII collected; KVKK/GDPR compliance in NFR-06; opaque session IDs only; consent notice required

gamePurpose: Develop COM0463 student practical SDLC management and risk decision-making skills through an immersive 3D office-building simulation (Bloom L3–L5)
gameSubject: SDLC lifecycle management, risk management, resource allocation, stakeholder communication, technical debt — aligned with Marchewka Chapters 6-11 and PMBOK Guide
gameMethod: Office materialization as visual reward for SDLC completion. Decision cards force trade-off analysis. 4-resource scarcity creates authentic pressure. AI Game Master generates contextual events that adapt to player state, ensuring unique learning paths.
gamePlayers: COM0463 IT Project Management students, Final Year, n≈35
gamePoints: +Score for resource preservation across phases. Budget saved = Budget score. Low TechDebt = TechDebt score. Phase completion = +50 per phase. Event survival = +10 per event.
gameAchievements: Office Architect: complete all 6 SDLC phases. Chaos Survivor: survive 10+ events without Game Over. Budget Guardian: finish with Budget > 70%. Zero Debt: finish with TechDebt < 15%.
gameBadges: Void Pioneer (Phase 1 complete), Code Commander (Phase 3 complete), Ship Captain (Phase 5 complete), Office Architect (all 6 phases), Master PM (Score ≥ 400)
gameMeasurement: Pre/post SDLC knowledge quiz (≥25% improvement target); SUS usability survey (≥80); Risk Register quality rubric on final project (compared to non-players); replay rate (target ≥2.5 sessions)
gameOverview: Void Studio is a browser-based 3D simulation for COM0463 where managing the SDLC correctly causes an office to materialize from a void. Players manage Budget, Morale, Technical Debt, and Time across 6 phases while resolving AI-generated or predefined crisis events. The visual metaphor — building reality through competent management — makes abstract PM concepts tangible.
